page: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is a shared-resource virtual server powered by the AMD EPYC processor family on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs operating at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz, coupled with 4.0 GB of system memory to form a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Running on the QEMU hypervisor, the processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. Advanced CPU instruction capabilities include AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Bundled storage is delivered via an integrated 80 GB local NVMe SSD, while no dedicated graphics accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate an asymmetric performance profile characterized by upper-quartile single-threaded speed contrasted with constrained parallel execution. In synthetic testing, the instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1939.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 3016.89, both ranking in the top 25 percent. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded metrics fall in the lower quartile, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 5189.05 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3520.0. Uncached memory throughput across 256 MB blocks remains moderate, registering 46.06 GB/sec for reads and 52.18 GB/sec for writes. Application throughput indicators recorded 4.02 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 3.66 GB/sec in static web serving, while lightweight 135M parameter LLM inference achieved 518.21 prompt tokens per second and 139.81 generation tokens per second.

The hardware configuration provides high operational efficiency for light workloads by combining low resource overhead, high-speed local NVMe storage, and strong single-core execution. The primary architectural tradeoff centers on shared CPU scheduling and a small 4.0 GB memory footprint, which restrict its utility for compute-intensive parallelism or large in-memory databases. The server is best suited for entry-level web serving, auxiliary microservices, staging environments, build workers, and lightweight task automation.
